pages.text: The holder scans its beam every half second, and the pumpjack assembles by itself as soon as every rule below is met. Nothing needs a click or a redstone signal.

$(li)The head and the connector must each be within $(item)6 blocks$() of the holder along the beam, with only hammer parts in between.$(li)Every part, the connector and the crank must face along the $(item)same axis$() as the holder. A part turned sideways ends the beam there.

$(li)The $(item)base$() must be in the same column as the head, $(item)1 to 8 blocks$() below it.$(li)The $(item)crank$() must be in the same column as the connector, $(item)1 to 7 blocks$() below it.$(li)Only one pumpjack can drive a given base.
If you remove the base or the crank, the beam disassembles back into blocks. Put the piece back and it reassembles on its own.
The $(item)large$() hammer parts, head and connector work the same way as the small ones and can replace them for a heavier look. With a large part above it, the holder widens automatically.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
